speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, could you tell me if the tremors in your hands occur when you are resting or only when you are trying to use your hands? Also, when did you first notice these memory issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any stiffness in your limbs or a noticeable slowing of your movements? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your sense of smell or difficulty with balance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty initiating movement or feel that your steps have become shorter and shuffling? I would also like to check for rigidity in your limbs during a physical examination.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, medicated with aspirin and amlodipine. Family history of schizophrenia in his mother. No other significant medical or psychiatric history. Social history: Drinks 1-2 beers nightly and is a former cigar smoker.

speaker: Doctor

I need to rule out vascular causes or other structural abnormalities given your history of hypertension and memory issues.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No acute abnormalities. Mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the resting tremor, bradykinesia, and mild cognitive decline with a normal MRI, I suspect Parkinson's disease with mild cognitive impairment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's disease
